title: APH credentialStatus entry (spec 6.3.3.1)
description: The OPTIONAL top-level `credentialStatus` member of a NotarizationEnvelope. It is a W3C BitstringStatusListEntry, and in APH it describes the status of the PARENT Delegation Mandate named by credentialSubject.policy.delegationMandateId - not the status of the envelope carrying it (spec 6.3.3.1). The member is OMITTED when absent and MUST NOT be emitted as null: an envelope with no status reference is byte-identical to a pre-revocation envelope, which is what keeps existing signatures valid (spec 7.1.1).

id.description: Identifier for this status entry. Omitted when absent.

type.description: Closed value. Spec 14.1 pins W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0 rather than accepting 'or equivalent': this value is signed wire content under the 7.1 strict parse, so two implementations reading different vintages of the same idea would both look conformant and would never interoperate.

statusPurpose.description: Closed value set of exactly one member (spec 6.3.3.5). 'suspension' is excluded because it is reversible and 6.3.2 forbids re-activation. An unrecognized purpose is a FAILURE, never a skip - a verifier that treated it as 'no status claim was made' would let any producer disable the check by writing a word that verifier has never seen.

statusListIndex.description: This mandate's position in the list, a base-10 integer IN A JSON STRING (spec 6.3.3.6). Never a JSON number: in runtimes where every JSON number is an IEEE-754 double, an index past 2^53 rounds silently and the verifier reads a DIFFERENT BIT - answering, with full confidence, a question about some other mandate. Index reuse is PROHIBITED (6.3.3.6).

statusListCredential.description: Absolute https: URL of the status list credential. MUST be same-origin - identical scheme, host and port - with the endpoint DERIVED from the notary's own did:web (spec 6.3.3.2). A verifier encountering a cross-origin or non-https value MUST reject the envelope and MUST NOT fetch the named URL. Same-origin deliberately permits a DIFFERENT PATH, which is how a notary points at a second list. NOTE: this constraint cannot be expressed in JSON Schema, because it relates this value to credentialSubject.notarization.notaryService.id elsewhere in the envelope; a schema pass is necessary and NOT sufficient.
